scope.requirements:
# Clean design specification
Ethereum NFT raffle; immutable factory, ERC-1167 clones with immutable implementation. One entry costs 1,000,000 units of canonical six-decimal USDC. One purchase mints a transferable ERC721 ticket representing a contiguous inclusive range. Exactly one ERC721 prize is escrowed atomically at creation. Reserve met awards NFT and 95% sponsor / 5% treasury. Reserve missed awards 80% gross to winner, 15% sponsor, 5% treasury. Refund outcome pays 100% per entry and returns prize. Rounding is floor on aggregate protocol fee; remainder must be allocated without loss. No administrator, mutable configuration or upgrade. Request window [sale end, end+2days); callback accepted strictly before request timestamp+2days. Refunds open at deadline. Callback records result only. Settlement is permissionless, storage-only; redemption requires current ticket owner, burns claim atomically, and must revert all effects on delivery failure. Sponsor and treasury can claim independently after settlement. Never move assets between raffle clones. Quote token and Chainlink wrapper are trusted canonical dependencies; arbitrary prize contracts and ticket recipients are untrusted. Frontend discovery is advisory; transaction decisions must reread current chain state.

This specification was composed before scanner results and historical findings. Source, not design prose, determines actual behavior. No tests, audit history, accepted-risk lists or scanner results are provided.

findings.title: LEAD L-01: Untrusted-prize requirement exceeds the interface's honest-ERC721 assumption
findings.description:
The clean requirements call arbitrary prize contracts untrusted, while IRaffle states that supported prizes are honest standards-compliant ERC721s. The factory checks self-reported ERC165 support, the receiver transition, and ownerOf after escrow; those checks cannot establish future transfer behavior. In a reserve-met result, settlement can allocate the full pot to sponsor and treasury independently of NFT delivery. If an admitted prize subsequently refuses transfer, redemption reverts atomically but NftWon has no refund transition. This is a concrete conditional liveness/trust-boundary path, not a demonstrated exploit or a finding against an honest compliant prize: no particular hostile prize implementation is present in the pinned context. Keep as a lead until the intended prize trust boundary and an applicable concrete prize behavior are established. Defensive obligation: state the supported prize trust assumptions explicitly and assess whether the intended winner exit must survive permanent prize-delivery failure.
Assumptions: DESIGN.md is authoritative for the requirement that arbitrary prize contracts are untrusted; interface comments are evidence of a narrower implementation assumption, not permission to narrow the audit.; The conditional delivery failure requires prize behavior not instantiated by a prize implementation in this context. No claim of an executed or confirmed loss path is made.; Canonical USDC and the configured Chainlink wrapper behave according to the stated trusted dependency model.

findings.title: C-01: Sponsor prize release can strand an NFT in a clone created after recipient validation
findings.description:
Post-seal correction of the original broad L-02 lead. Raffle A can be initialized with a sponsorRecipient address that is not yet deployed or registered and differs from A and the fixed forbidden addresses. RaffleFactory subsequently creates and registers raffle B at that address using Clones.clone/CREATE. If A enters Refunding or CashWon, releaseSponsorPrize sends A's configured NFT to the stored recipient using transferFrom without re-evaluating _isProtocolDestination. An ordinary ERC721 transfer bypasses B's restrictive onERC721Received hook, and ownerOf correctly reports B, so A marks the prize claimed. Where B has a distinct configured prize, its release methods cannot return A's unrelated NFT and there is no generic rescue path. This is a source-supported same-factory no-assets-between-clones invariant violation, requiring deliberate or mistaken future-clone recipient configuration. Impact is the sponsor-directed prize becoming stranded; no ability to redirect a correctly configured unrelated user's claim, steal another raffle's USDC, or contaminate B's accounted pot was found. Confidence is in this conditional source path; no deployment, address calculation or executable reproduction was performed. Defensive property: NFT release should apply the intended current-destination policy consistently, while the design explicitly handles the liveness consequences of an immutable recipient that becomes ineligible.
Assumptions: The sponsor-selected future clone recipient is unregistered/code-less at A initialization, distinct from A and all fixed forbidden destinations.; The factory later successfully deploys B at that address before A's prize release; B's configured prize differs from A's returned prize.; A reaches Refunding or CashWon and its prize has ordinary ERC721 transferFrom semantics.; The explicit no-assets-between-raffle-clones requirement applies to sponsor-configured recipients. Severity is low because no unauthorized redirection of an unrelated correctly configured claim is established.

Existing tests are excluded by explicit sourceOnly=true, existingTests=false scope. Docker daemon is unavailable and no pinned local tool image was verified, so the separately conditional test-inclusive plan is blocked and no host-tool fallback is authorized.

All five production files including IRaffle.sol and IRaffleFactory.sol were reviewed in full from this exact context. Dependencies were snapshotted in full; manual semantic review focused on reachable ERC721 ownership/mint/burn, SafeERC20 transfer, clone creation, reentrancy storage, Math.mulDiv and VRF base/authentication. Remaining library utility text was not exhaustively audited.

Root pnpm-lock.yaml is fully pinned; only the relevant contracts importer and Chainlink/OpenZeppelin resolution entries were semantically inspected. Package declarations identify @chainlink/contracts 1.5.0 and @openzeppelin/contracts 5.6.1. No registry provenance or deployed canonical address was verified.

L-02 (unconfirmed integration lead): destination checks recognize the current factory and its already registered clones, not every other-factory or not-yet-created clone. Raffle.sol 593-604 and RaffleFactory.sol 154-168 need a precise interpretation of never move assets between raffle clones. No unauthorized victim-loss path is established; deliberate selection or transfer to an unreachable address is not promoted to a vulnerability.

USDC administrative freeze/blacklisting and a permanently non-cooperating prize can obstruct their respective transfers; transaction atomicity preserves recorded claims on revert but cannot guarantee delivery by a third-party asset contract.

NFT payout uses transferFrom plus ownerOf verification, not a receiver hook. This avoids a receiver veto but relies on the owner-selected or immutable recipient being capable of managing the received NFT; no unsupported claim that every contract recipient can recover it is made.

No frontend, deployed contract state, production credentials, historical report, scanner result, prior test source, memory or peer conclusion was used for this original pass. Target SHA is operator-supplied and exact selected bytes are bound by the native snapshot; source git history was not inspected.

Local model selection is gpt-6-astra with ultra effort as provided by the active runner instruction; provider-returned model and effort fields are unknown. No provider adapter or fallback was used. External usage, cost and provider identity are not independently verified by Gebal.

This is an append-only post-seal reconciliation of independent same-model source reviews. FIRST-PASS.md, review.original.json and their SEAL.json remain unchanged. The original source-only review and this addendum use the exact same context and snapshot hashes.

L-01 remains an informational trust-assumption lead. Accounting specialist proposed high/medium confidence; lifecycle specialist proposed medium/medium confidence. The raw original responses and their seals are preserved. Conditional prize refusal is source-supported, but the specification does not explicitly promise a recovery policy for every permanently hostile NFT, and no particular hostile implementation is present. Atomic rollback on delivery failure is satisfied. No high-severity confirmed defect is asserted.

C-01 refines the originally unresolved L-02 using the missing current-destination check specifically on sponsor NFT release. Other-factory destinations remain a separate unresolved scope interpretation; they are not needed for C-01.

Source-only conclusions remain unexecuted. Docker unavailable, no verified pinned local image, unsupported gas_reports key, and compiler 0.8.36 outside the harness's documented integration-tested versions block stronger execution claims. No cold review was imported into a different test-inclusive context.

All observations remain needs-review; no human accept/reject decision was recorded. Supplemental specialists and skeptical adjudication are external assistant stages, not capabilities natively orchestrated or provenance-verified by Gebal.
